authority: Superintendence Co. of India (P) Ltd. v. Krishan Murgai (SC, 1980)
appliesWhen: the restraint on joining a competitor or similar business operates AFTER employment ends
doesNotApplyWhen: the restraint operates DURING the subsisting employment only (Niranjan Golikari v. Century Spinning, SC, 1967)
plainEnglish: Agreements in restraint of trade are void in India. A clause stopping you from joining a competitor, working in the same field, or starting a similar business after you leave is unenforceable however it is worded, and however senior the role.
negotiationAsk: Ask for the post-employment restraint to be deleted, or narrowed so it applies only while you remain employed.

authority: Niranjan Shankarrao Golikari v. Century Spinning & Mfg. Co. (SC, 1967)
appliesWhen: the restraint on competing or moonlighting operates only DURING the term of employment
plainEnglish: Restraints that apply only while you are still employed by the company are generally enforceable in India, unlike restraints that try to bind you after you leave.
negotiationAsk: Confirm in writing that the restriction ends on your last working day.

appliesWhen: the clause restrains soliciting former colleagues or clients after employment, without restraining your own right to work
plainEnglish: Non-solicitation clauses are treated differently from non-compete clauses by Indian courts. They do not stop you from working, only from actively poaching the employer's clients or staff, and are more likely to be enforced if reasonable in scope and duration.
negotiationAsk: Ask for a fixed, short duration (6-12 months) and a definition limited to clients you personally serviced.

appliesWhen: the clause absolutely restricts your right to enforce your rights through the ordinary courts or tribunals, or sets a limitation period shorter than the law allows
doesNotApplyWhen: the clause only names which specific court has territorial jurisdiction, without removing your right to approach a court at all
plainEnglish: A clause that completely bars you from going to court, or from approaching a labour authority, to enforce your rights is void. Naming a particular city's courts as the agreed venue is different and is usually valid.
negotiationAsk: Ask for the clause to be reworded so it only fixes venue, not your right to sue.

appliesWhen: the clause purports to make arbitration the exclusive remedy for disputes that a labour court, industrial tribunal, or statutory authority (e.g. gratuity, provident fund, POSH) has jurisdiction over by law
plainEnglish: Parties can agree to arbitrate ordinary contractual disputes, but they cannot contract out of a statutory forum (like a labour court or the authority under the Payment of Gratuity Act) that the law gives you the right to approach.
negotiationAsk: Ask for statutory claims to be expressly carved out of the arbitration clause.

section: Section 12(5) read with the Seventh Schedule
authority: Perkins Eastman Architects DPC v. HSCC (India) Ltd. (SC, 2019)
appliesWhen: the arbitrator is to be appointed unilaterally by the employer, or by an employee/officer of the employer, or is named as the employer itself
plainEnglish: A person who has an interest in the outcome of the dispute, or who is appointed unilaterally by one side, cannot act as the arbitrator. An employer naming itself, its MD, or an employee as the sole arbitrator is invalid; you can ask a court to appoint an independent arbitrator instead.
negotiationAsk: Ask for a neutral appointment mechanism, e.g. appointment by an arbitral institution or by mutual agreement.

appliesWhen: the clause fixes a payment owed if you resign before a minimum tenure, or fails to buy out a training bond period
plainEnglish: A sum stated in the contract as payable on breach is treated as an upper cap on compensation, not a penalty the employer can automatically collect in full. The employer can only recover its actual, reasonably proven loss (e.g. documented training cost), even if the contract states a larger fixed figure.
negotiationAsk: Ask the employer to itemise the actual training cost the bond is meant to recover, and cap the bond amount to that figure.

appliesWhen: the clause implies the employer can force you to continue working, or seek a court order compelling your continued service
plainEnglish: Contracts of personal service cannot be specifically enforced in India. If you resign in breach of contract, the employer's remedy is damages, not an order compelling you to keep working.

appliesWhen: the clause purports to waive, reduce, or make discretionary the payment of statutory gratuity after 5 years of continuous service
plainEnglish: Gratuity after 5 years of continuous service (with the usual exceptions for death or disablement) is a statutory entitlement at eligible establishments. A contract clause cannot waive it or make it conditional on employer discretion; the Act overrides any inconsistent contract term.
negotiationAsk: Ask for the clause to be deleted; gratuity applies by law regardless of what the offer letter says.

appliesWhen: you fall within the wage threshold the Act covers and the clause purports to waive the statutory minimum bonus
plainEnglish: Where the Payment of Bonus Act applies to your role and establishment, the statutory minimum bonus cannot be contracted away. Note that many salaried, managerial roles above the Act's wage ceiling are outside its coverage entirely, and any 'bonus' in that case is purely contractual.
negotiationAsk: Confirm in writing whether you are covered by the Act; if you are, the statutory minimum applies regardless of contract wording.

statute: Employees' Provident Funds and Miscellaneous Provisions Act, 1952
appliesWhen: the clause allows the employer to reduce your wages to offset its statutory PF contribution, or treats PF enrolment as optional where the Act makes it mandatory
plainEnglish: At establishments covered by the EPF Act, the employer cannot cut your pay to fund its own share of the provident fund contribution, and cannot make enrolment optional once you are covered.
negotiationAsk: Ask for confirmation that PF contribution is on top of, not carved out of, the stated CTC.

appliesWhen: the clause provides maternity leave or benefits below the statutory minimum (26 weeks for the first two children), or purports to let the employer terminate on account of pregnancy
plainEnglish: Maternity benefits under this Act are a floor, not a ceiling that can be negotiated down. Any contract term less favourable than the Act is void to that extent, and the Act overrides it automatically.
negotiationAsk: Ask for the clause to be aligned with, or simply silent on (letting the Act govern), the statutory entitlement.

appliesWhen: the clause allows the employer open-ended or unlisted deductions from wages beyond the categories the Act permits (e.g. fines, absence, damage to employer property, statutory dues, authorised recoveries)
plainEnglish: Deductions from wages are restricted by law to specific permitted categories and are subject to caps and procedure (e.g. a fine requires prior notice and a hearing). A blanket 'we may deduct any amount owed' clause is enforceable only to the extent it tracks what the Act actually permits.
negotiationAsk: Ask for the deduction clause to list specific, permitted categories rather than an open-ended right to deduct.

statute: Sexual Harassment of Women at Workplace (Prevention, Prohibition and Redressal) Act, 2013
appliesWhen: the clause routes harassment or workplace-safety complaints exclusively through HR, management, or arbitration, bypassing the statutory Internal Committee
plainEnglish: Every establishment with 10 or more employees must have an Internal Committee to receive and inquire into complaints of sexual harassment. A contract cannot substitute a different, employer-controlled channel for this statutory mechanism.
negotiationAsk: Ask the employer to confirm the Internal Committee's composition and that this clause does not override it.

section: Section 27 (restraint-of-trade principle) and Section 23 (lawful consideration and object)
appliesWhen: the clause assigns to the employer all IP you create at any time, including outside working hours, unrelated to the employer's business, and using no employer resources
plainEnglish: IP created within the scope of your employment, using company resources or time, is standard for the employer to own. A clause reaching personal projects that have nothing to do with your job or the company's business is broader than what is typically enforced, though it is not automatically void.
negotiationAsk: Ask for the assignment to be limited to work created within the scope of employment or using company resources.

section: Section 23 (unconscionability as a factor; not a standalone voiding provision)
appliesWhen: the notice period, or the buyout cost of notice, you owe on resignation is materially longer or costlier than what the employer owes you on termination without cause
plainEnglish: Freedom of contract generally permits asymmetric notice periods in India, and this is common. It is lawful but one-sided, and worth flagging and negotiating rather than accepting silently.
negotiationAsk: Ask for symmetric notice periods, or for the buyout formula to be identical in both directions.

section: Model Standing Orders on termination and misconduct procedure
appliesWhen: the clause allows termination 'for cause' or 'for misconduct' without any inquiry, show-cause notice, or opportunity to respond, and you are a 'workman' under the Industrial Disputes Act
doesNotApplyWhen: you are in a managerial or supervisory role that falls outside the statutory definition of 'workman'
plainEnglish: Where you qualify as a 'workman', dismissal for misconduct without a fair inquiry can be challenged even if the contract purports to allow summary termination. Whether you qualify as a 'workman' depends on your actual duties, not your job title, and that is a factual question this tool cannot resolve from the document alone.

appliesWhen: the clause allows the employer to extend probation indefinitely, or an unlimited number of times, at its sole discretion
plainEnglish: Open-ended probation extension clauses are common and generally lawful, but they leave you without the fuller notice or process protections a confirmed employee gets, for an unbounded period.
negotiationAsk: Ask for a maximum cumulative probation period and a defined confirmation review date.

appliesWhen: the clause allows the employer to transfer you to any location in India, or to any group company, at its discretion
plainEnglish: Broad transfer clauses are standard in Indian employment contracts and are generally enforceable, though they can be negotiated, especially for a specific role tied to one city.
negotiationAsk: Ask for the transfer clause to be scoped to the same city or function, or for relocation support to be specified.

appliesWhen: the clause requires you to indemnify the employer for a broad, undefined range of losses, including losses the employer's own negligence contributed to
plainEnglish: One-sided indemnity clauses are lawful under freedom of contract, but an indemnity that is not capped, or that covers the employer's own fault, is unusually broad.
negotiationAsk: Ask for the indemnity to be capped, mutual, and to exclude losses caused by the employer's own negligence or breach.

section: Section 27 (does not apply to genuine confidentiality obligations, only to restraints on trade)
appliesWhen: the confidentiality obligation survives termination for a defined or indefinite period, protecting genuine trade secrets
doesNotApplyWhen: the 'confidentiality' clause is actually a disguised restraint on using your general skill, knowledge, and experience elsewhere
plainEnglish: Unlike non-competes, confidentiality obligations protecting genuine trade secrets can validly survive employment, even indefinitely. The line matters: your general skill and know-how is yours to take with you; the employer's specific confidential information is not.
negotiationAsk: Ask for the clause to define 'confidential information' narrowly and exclude your general skills and experience.
